displays.title: Set up a display
displays.intro: The Throne Display is a small round desk screen (ESP32-C3, 240x240) that shows your agents working around the Emperor's throne, their health and the latest messages, live. Plug it into this computer with a USB cable and this page installs the firmware, connects it to Wi-Fi and gives it its own read-only key. You never copy a token.
displays.unsupported: Requires Chrome or Edge on a computer (Web Serial). Phones, Safari and Firefox can't talk to USB devices; you can still set the display up from its own Wi-Fi setup page (hold the screen for 5 seconds).
displays.connectHint: Plug the display into this computer, then pick it in the browser's list (it shows up as a USB JTAG/serial device).
displays.installHint: Installing keeps the display's saved settings. It takes about a minute; don't unplug the cable.
displays.looking: The display is looking for networks...
displays.band24Hint: The list comes from the display itself, so it only shows 2.4 GHz networks. The display can't use 5 GHz Wi-Fi; if your router has separate 2.4 and 5 GHz names, pick the 2.4 GHz one.
displays.openNetworkHint: Leave empty for an open network
displays.displayNameHint: Shown in the list of displays below, so you can revoke the right one later.

displays.timedOutUsbLost: The display restarted and the USB connection did not come back, and it hasn't reached the server yet. Look at the screen: a green dot near the top right means it is live; "Joining Wi-Fi" or a red dot means it could not connect.
displays.timedOut: The display hasn't reached the server yet. Check the Wi-Fi password and that {host} is reachable from that network.
displays.yourDisplaysIntro: Each display has its own read-only key. Revoke it when a display leaves your desk.

page.title: Settings
page.description: Manage your profile, workspace, and connections.

connections.startTitle: Start with an agent or a team
connections.startBody: Use the guided setup in Agents. Choose a role, or a ready-made team with a shared chat. Manual runtime guides are below if you already run your own agents.

hermes.title: Hermes agents
hermes.body: Use one Hermes profile and one bridge service per Emperor agent. Best when your team runs Hermes on local machines or Raspberry Pi-style workers.

openclaw.title: OpenClaw agents
openclaw.body: Use the OpenClaw plugin when you want the packaged local workspace and doctor/repair commands.

connections.operatorRuleBody: Create the agent profile in Emperor first, then connect exactly one local runtime profile or workspace to that agent. The runtime can be Hermes or OpenClaw; Emperor should stay runtime-neutral.
connections.quickSetupTitle: Quick Setup — Let your own LLM configure it
connections.quickSetupBody: Don't want to configure everything manually? Copy a prompt below, paste it into Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, or any LLM, and it will walk you through the entire setup — installing the runtime, configuring the bridge, writing bootstrap files, and tailoring the agent to your role.
connections.replaceRole: Replace {placeholder} with your agent's actual role — e.g. "SEO Specialist", "Lead Generation Agent", "Technical Implementation Agent". The more specific you are, the better the result.

tokens.name: Token name
tokens.namePlaceholder: e.g. Pi bridge, Growth agent, QA runtime

help.read_only: For a screen or dashboard that shows what your agents are doing. It can only read the live agent feed (GET /api/mcp/live); it cannot send messages or change anything.
help.requests: For another platform that sends work to your agents (a "send task to agent" button). It can only create requests and read their status; the token name is shown to agents as the source.
help.mcp_danger: For trusted local runtimes that need managed secret leasing. Use sparingly.
help.mcp_full: Default token for connected agents, bridges, and normal runtime access.

tokens.callbackHint: Emperor posts a signed update here whenever a request changes status. Stored encrypted.
tokens.copyNow: Copy it now. Emperor will not show this secret again.
tokens.activeIntro: Revoke anything that is no longer attached to a real runtime.
tokens.empty: No access tokens active. Create one to connect an agent runtime.
tokens.mcpTitle: Connect Claude, Codex, or another MCP client
tokens.mcpBody: Emperor exposes a real Model Context Protocol server at /mcp — point any MCP-capable client at it with an Agent access token from above to get every agent/task/project/Knowledge & Rules/messaging tool, plus your company's operating doctrine, automatically.
tokens.claudeDesktopHint: Edit this in Claude Desktop's config file directly.
tokens.claudeWebBody: Add a custom connector and paste just the URL above — no manual Client ID/Secret needed. Emperor registers Claude automatically and you'll be asked to approve the connection while logged in here; no separate token is required for this path.
tokens.claudeWebHttps: Requires this instance to be served over HTTPS (a reverse proxy with a real certificate — Caddy, nginx, Cloudflare Tunnel). Self-hosted installs on plain HTTP (e.g. a LAN IP with no proxy) should use the manual token method above instead.

advanced.title: Advanced runtime setup
advanced.intro: Use this when manually validating a local companion, bridge, heartbeats, checkpoints, or token permissions. Most operators only need the runtime guides above.
advanced.scopesBody: Agent access maps to the normal MCP access scope. Secret leasing maps to the privileged scope required for managed secret leases and should only be used on trusted runtimes.

connect.title: Connect a host
connect.description: Run this on the Linux machine (with systemd) where your Hermes agents run, as the same user that runs them (not root). It installs emperor-hermes {version}, checks its checksum and connects the machine. Agents already running there are found automatically.
connect.connectedHint: Its agents show up on the host card within a minute.
connect.insecureWarning: Emperor is open over plain http at a public address, so the host's key would travel unencrypted. The command refuses that; use https, or add --insecure at the end if you accept the risk.
connect.oneTimeHint: The code works once. The host gets its own key, separate from agent tokens; you can revoke it here at any time.

actions.title: Actions
actions.intro: Choose what {who} may do on its own. Ask first sends each call to your Inbox and the agent waits; approving lets that exact call run once. Off refuses it.
actions.scopeNote: Only the actions listed here are governed. Anything else an agent can do in Emperor (reading, uploading files, deleting tasks, answering a message it was sent...) is not affected by these settings.
actions.companyHint: Every agent uses these unless its own setting says otherwise.
actions.adminsOnly: Only owners and admins can change permissions.

scope.adminsOnly: Only owners and admins can change this agent's scope.
scope.dataScopeHint: Restrict which customers and projects this agent can read or act on — tasks, artifacts, and Knowledge & Rules under them. Team chat stays visible regardless of scope.
scope.lockedOut: No customers or projects selected — this agent will see nothing until you add at least one.
scope.agentsHint: Choose which other agents {name} can reach. This works one way: it limits only {name}, not the agents you leave out. They can still message it, and it always sees itself.
scope.allHint: {name} can see, message and hand work to every agent in the company, including new ones.
scope.noneSelected: No agents selected — {name} will work alone: it won't see, message or hand work to any other agent.

create.hermesPrereq: Hermes requires a running bridge on your machine. You'll need Python 3.10+, the Hermes CLI, and an LLM API key. The setup guide appears right after creation — no terminal expertise needed.
create.apiKeysHint: Hermes reads keys from ~/.hermes/.env or your environment. EmperorClaw only stores the provider choice as metadata — the bridge reads it to auto-detect which LLM you're using.
create.noLocal: {provider} does not support same-server deployment yet
create.llmProviderHint: Which LLM does this agent use? Stored as metadata — the bridge reads it to auto-detect the provider. API keys must be configured in the runtime environment (~/.hermes/.env), not in EmperorClaw.
create.afterHost: Emperor sets it up on {host} and shows the progress here. It is online in a few minutes.
create.afterHermes: 1. Configure your LLM API key in ~/.hermes/.env  2. Start the Hermes bridge  3. Agent appears online
create.afterOther: 1. Configure your runtime  2. Point it to EmperorClaw's MCP endpoint  3. Agent registers on first heartbeat

setup.startLocalHint: Emperor uses this agent’s saved provider and key, installs Hermes, and connects it automatically. Retry this profile if the first setup failed.
setup.createdConnectHere: Agent created — connect on this server
setup.onlineProcessing: {name} is online and processing tasks on {provider}. Bridge is active.
setup.configuredLocal: {name} is configured as a {role} running on {provider} on this machine. Run the commands below directly — no SSH needed.

setup.stepDownload: Download and verify the installer on the host (Linux with systemd):

setup.stepConnectHost: Then connect the machine under Settings → Runtime hosts to restart it from here.

setup.tokenHint: Click Generate token to insert a real token, or replace {placeholder} with one from Settings → Access Tokens.
